What do you do when you're not ready to check "Done" when asked if you believe in faith?

Whether we encounter LDS theology, explore different practices, or the host explains how they came to a certain point in their faith journey. The conversation around religion feels centered not around lived reality but on endless apologetic arguments which, after a while, lead people to forget the solemness of practice. Whatever tradition you come from and wherever you are going, you are welcome here to sit and engage.


Gen Z will likely never be as religious as our forefathers, but like all humans we wish to seek something beyond ourselves.

title: REAL LIFE WITH LAN
author: REAL LIFE WITH LAN
description:
Real life. Real lessons. Real rebuilding.

Welcome to Real Life With Lan — the podcast about what happens when life doesn’t go according to plan…and you decide to build what’s next anyway.

I’m Lani, aka Lan — a wife, mom of three, entrepreneur and woman rebuilding from the inside out.

After 20+ years in business, sales, leadership, real estate, speaking, training and entrepreneurship, I’ve experienced wins, losses, pivots and plenty of lessons learned the hard way.

Now I’m navigating a new chapter: deepening my relationship with God, rebuilding my health, finding myself again, changing my relationship with money, raising my family and learning how to turn decades of experience into opportunities in today’s digital world.

We’ll talk faith, health, healing, marriage, motherhood, money, business, personal growth, food, family and the beautiful chaos in between.

I’m not here because I have life figured out.

I’m letting you watch me build what’s next.

If you’re rebuilding too, pull up a chair. You belong here.

Starting over doesn’t mean starting from zero.

On Just Show Up, host Christian Thompson talks with friends, family, and people whose big stories started small about what they almost didn't start, what their first small step looked like, and what showing up looks like on a bad day. title: Synapse & Cognition
author: Aima Aamir
description:
Synapse & Cognition explores how the brain and mind shape the way we think, feel and behave. Each episode takes a question we rarely stop to ask, like "Why do we say men don't cry?", and looks at it through psychology and neuroscience, drawing on research, real studies and conversations with students, researchers and academics.
From emotion and memory to sleep and the teenage brain, the show asks what the evidence says, where it's still debated, and what it means for everyday life. No jargon without explanation, and no claims without evidence.
Hosted by Aima Aamir. New episodes are released regularly.

title: Super CMO Show

description:
Hosted by Sivaraman Swaminathan (Swami), the Super CMO Show explores the ideas, decisions, and practices shaping marketing. Through in-depth conversations with marketing leaders, academics, authors, and entrepreneurs, the show uncovers how businesses understand customers, build brands, and drive growth.

From consumer behaviour and brand strategy to marketing technology, data, AI, and emerging trends, each episode connects fresh thinking with practical experience. We explore the why behind marketing decisions, the mental models guiding successful marketers, and the lessons our guests have learned along the way.

Whether you are a seasoned marketing leader, an entrepreneur building your business, or a student beginning your career, these conversations will challenge your assumptions, broaden your perspective, and help you become a more thoughtful and effective marketer.

title: The Middle Space

Through honest conversations about embodied health, we explore the space between science and story, medicine and humanity, and evidence and lived experience. Join naturopathic doctor Stacy Rempel as she dives into the complexity of health, healing, and what helps us truly flourish.

title: Stats We Barely Understand Pod

title: Rise With Veronik'A
author: Veronik'A
description:
"Rise with Veronik'A"
Life is not only about success, perfect choices, and easy transformations. It is also made of fear, doubt, loss, illness, disability, loneliness, failure, grief, relationships, ambition, courage, unexpected detours, and sometimes moments when simply moving forward already feels difficult.
"Rise with Veronik'A" is a podcast about all of it.
Through honest reflections, real stories, meaningful conversations, and practical tools, Veronik'A explores the experiences that shape the way we think, feel, love, choose, and live.
We will talk about self-confidence, self-esteem, the power of words, relationships, resilience, memory, ambition, and personal growth.
But we will also make space for conversations that are still too often avoided: mental health, illness, disability, grief, exclusion, vulnerability, and those life experiences that can change everything.
Not to offer ready-made answers.  
Not to pretend that every difficulty can be solved through positive thinking.
But to understand more deeply, question what we have been taught, listen differently, and discover what can truly help us move forward.
Some episodes will inspire you. Others will challenge you. And some may simply make you feel understood.
Because rising does not always mean becoming stronger.
Sometimes, it means accepting.  
Sometimes, rebuilding.  
Sometimes, changing direction.  
And sometimes, simply finding the courage to take the next step.
Think differently. Rise stronger. Live fully.

title: Dropped In: The Cost of Caregiving
author: Christy Russell
description:
I was not prepared to become a care coordinator, expert in education, medical, legal, and future planning jargon overnight. 
I hated feeling like an imposter who didn't have my sh!t together, and didn't know how to help my son. 
So I spent the next 15 years working inside the systems that support neurodivergent and disabled kids. 
I sat in the rooms where decisions get made. 
Dropped In: The Cost of Caregiving are the stories I needed to hear when my son first got diagnosed, and what I need now that he's 18 and facing the "cliff."

From its origins to the highly anticipated 2026 edition, we will uncover the stories, behind-the-scenes moments, innovative techniques, and delightful anecdotes that have made this event the "Olympus" of the cocoa world. Episode 1: The Origin of the Legend – The Genesis of the Competition
Episode 2: The Olympus of Pastry Chefs – Rules and Pressure

title: The Bitcoin Dialectic
author: Digvijay Chand Yaduka
description:
Stress-testing ideas shaping the future of money.
Bitcoin is the most radical monetary experiment in centuries. No one knows how it will play out. 
And yet, Bitcoin discourse often behaves like a courtroom where the verdict has already been decided. There's very little space left for intellectual uncertainty.
This podcast creates that space. No cheerleading. No dismissal. Just rigorous, adversarial curiosity. The Socratic Method, applied to Bitcoin.
Engineer (IIT Bombay) | Cognitive Scientist (Uni of Vienna)

title: Lou Uninterrupted
author: Deetra B Louis
description: What do you say when you pick the mic back up after years of silence? For me, it starts with an apology—and an honest conversation. If you knew me as Dreka from Melanated in Seattle, this is where we reconnect. If you’re meeting me for the first time, welcome to Lou, Uninterrupted. In this first episode, I reintroduce myself, revisit Melanated in Seattle, and acknowledge the way I disappeared. I share what it means to return on my own, with Yah as my lead, and get into accountability, uncomfortable realizations, and being honest with ourselves about the things we’re finally beginning to see. It’s easy to say we’re growing. But can we look at ourselves honestly enough to recognize where we still have work to do? Pull up a seat. I’ve got some catching up to do.

author: Weirding Way Media

Harrison Ford has been a smuggler, an archaeologist, a replicant hunter, a president, and the guy who shot first — and for half a century he's been the most reliable movie star in the world. He got there almost by accident. Never Tell Me the Odds works through his entire theatrical career one film at a time, from American Graffiti to the legacy sequels, tracing how a working carpenter who'd nearly quit acting became the face of the modern blockbuster.

Hosted by Chris Stachiw — the Doctor of Podcasting — with Mike White of The Projection Booth and Richard Hatem of Richard Hatem's Paranormal Bookshelf, the show works through the films in order: the blockbusters, the prestige pictures, the flops, and the ones even Ford probably forgot, with guests dropping in along the way. description:

From officiating iconic matches like The Rock vs. Hulk Hogan at WrestleMania X8 to unforgettable encounters like Goldberg vs. The Undertaker, Mike has been part of some of the biggest, most memorable, and most controversial moments in WWE history.

Now, he’s pulling back the curtain and sharing stories you’ve never heard before!

Join Mike as he reveals behind-the-scenes WWE secrets, untold stories about wrestling’s biggest superstars, what REALLY happens inside the ring, and what life was like working alongside Vince McMahon and other legendary figures.

He’ll also share his unfiltered opinions on today’s biggest WWE, AEW, and TNA wrestling news, revisit historic matches, and answer questions wrestling fans have always wanted to ask a WWE referee.

When Sir Amyas Leigh sets sail as a privateer under the flag of Queen Elizabeth, he plunges into a world of danger, treasure, and uncharted love. As he navigates fierce battles and encounters with pirates, Amyas must also confront the complexities of his heart, vying for the affections of the enchanting Mary. Will his thirst for glory overshadow his quest for true love?

In 'Westward Ho!', Charles Kingsley weaves a rich tapestry of swashbuckling escapades and heartfelt connections. Listeners will feel the thrill of the high seas and the pull of deep emotions, all while grappling with the broader themes of loyalty and honor. This audiobook invites you to explore the tension between duty and desire, as well as the allure of adventure that beckons from beyond the horizon. Discover what it means to be brave, to love fiercely, and to chase dreams across the waves.

title: A Journey Through Loss and Litigation
author: Roskilly & Co
description:
A Journey Through Loss and Litigation is a podcast series from Roskilly & Co exploring the challenges that can arise when grief, family relationships and contentious probate disputes intersect. 
In each episode, we speak with leading legal and other professionals about the realities of navigating disputes following the death of a loved one. Our guests share their expertise, practical advice and top tips, covering everything from contentious probate and inheritance claims to grief, mental health and the wider support available to those going through difficult circumstances.

title: NO FILTER
author: Black Parker
description:
NO FILTER by Black Parker — Podcast 

No scripts. No pretending. No filter.

NO FILTER with Black Parker is a short-form podcast built on real conversations about faith, life, relationships, personal growth, struggles, and the lessons we learn along the way.

In just a few minutes, Black Parker gets straight to the point—sharing his perspective, experiences, and thoughts on the things many people experience but don’t always talk about.

These aren’t hour-long conversations filled with filler. Each episode delivers one message, one perspective, and something to think about as you move through your day.

Sometimes it’s encouraging. Sometimes it’s challenging. Sometimes it’s uncomfortable. But it’s always real.

🎙️ Real life. Real faith. Real conversations. NO FILTER.

New episodes of NO FILTER with Black Parker — short enough to fit into your day, meaningful enough to stay on your mind.

title: Dry Bones: Voices of the Mid-Mon Valley
author: Phil Pagliari
description: The Valley of Dry Bones is a podcast with Pastor Phil Pagliari from the Mid-Mon Valley of Pennsylvania. Like Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, the Mon Valley needs new life. Each week Phil talks Scripture, preaching, faith, family, business, and Valley life with guests telling their real stories, all from a biblical perspective. Can these bones live? From Belle Vernon, PA.

title: Hotter by the Minute
author: Hotter by the Minute
description: This podcast is a conversation between two friends sharing honest, real-life experiences of being women over 50. We talk openly about the challenges no one prepares us for—aging, balancing family and work, changing identities, self-worth, and navigating both the hard days and the joyful ones. Through these conversations, we remind ourselves and other women that this stage of life is powerful. We are capable, resilient, and worthy, and at any age, we can still do anything, be anyone, and love ourselves exactly as we are.

title: Behind the Feed
author: Owen Fletcher
description: Behind the Feed is about the work behind a podcast feed — the tools, pipelines, and production choices that turn raw audio into published episodes. We talk about media generation, episode artwork, teasers, and the systems that keep a daily publishing schedule running without chaos.

title: Fortress Forward Insights
author: Fortress Group
description:
Exploring the ideas, innovations, and industry shifts shaping the future of digital infrastructure.


Hosted by Fortress Group, Fortress Forward Insights brings together industry experts, technology leaders, and innovators for conversations on the challenges and opportunities transforming telecommunications, fiber networks, power infrastructure, and beyond.


From emerging technologies and evolving infrastructure demands to real-world solutions, we go beyond the headlines to uncover what's changing, why it matters, and what's next.


Forward-thinking conversations. Real industry insights. The future of infrastructure.

title: The Future Of Sport, Reimagined
author: Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities
description:
We ask young people to show up for sport. What would it look like for sport to show up for them?


That's the question hosts Fallon and Victoria are exploring in this new podcast from The Walrus Lab, supported by Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities. Joined by athletes, community leaders, researchers and innovators, they bring a fresh perspective to conversations about the future of sport in Canada. Together, they explore what makes young people feel like they belong, how we can create more opportunities for girls to lead, and the ideas opening up new possibilities for participation.


From the impact of sport on our communities to the innovations changing how we play, each episode offers a new way to think about what sport can be—and how we can make it better.

Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

title: Satsang with Shambhavi
author: Shambhavi Sarasvati
description:
Join Shambhavi Sarasvati for a weekly exploration of self-realization, death, love, devotion, and waking up while living in a messy world. Satsang is an ancient spiritual practice from India. It means "being in reality together." During satsang, people gather with a teacher to learn, ask questions, find community, chant and sing. Shambhavi gives satsang in Portland, Oregon and elsewhere. The dharma talks offered here are recordings of the live satsang.  

Shambhavi is the spiritual director of Jaya Kula, a nonprofit organization. Her training is in the View and practices of Trika Shaivism from Kashmir and the Dzogchen tradition of Tibet. She is a householder sannyasini and a devotee of Anandamayi Ma. Visit jayakula.org for her full teaching schedule and more information.

Shambhavi's books include Mother Poems and A Crack in Time (2025), The Reality Sutras: Seeking the Heart of Trika Shaivism (2018), Tantra: the Play of Awakening (2012), Pilgrims to Openness: Direct Realization Tantra in Everyday Life (2009), Returning  (2015), and No Retreat: Poems on the Way to Waking Up (2016). All of Shambhavi's books are available on Amazon.

title: The Heroes of Sanctuary Farm – The Audio Drama Book 1
author: Manfred Zangl
description:
At Meadowbrook Sanctuary Farm, siblings Vanessa and Sebastian live with their parents and lots of rescued animals. But the farm is in danger! Together with Luna the dog, Emil the goat, Boris the hare, Roberto the bull and a very grumpy goblin, they set out on an adventure full of courage, friendship and chaos. An audio drama for kids aged 6 and up – each episode is a chapter from the book “The Heroes of Sanctuary Farm – Book 1: The Goblin in the Barn” by Manfred Zangl.

title: Jester's Privilege
author: Jester's Privilege
description:
Long ago, in the great halls of Europe, kings were surrounded by flattering courtiers too afraid to tell them the truth. But in every court, one man dared: the jester. With a jest, he showed the crown its folly, and while the court laughed, the king listened.

The King of kings and Lord of lords needs no jester. But to his church, he gave the keys of the kingdom. She is dearly loved, yet she can wander, and she has courtiers of her own.

Paul says we are fools for Christ. So, as servants of the true King, we've put on the motley to laugh at ourselves, speak the truth in love, and call the church to listen to her King.

This is Jester's Privilege.

https://jestersprivilegepodcast.com

title: Your’s sonderly
author: Malli
description:
I’m an ordinary person, curious about other people’s lives and the stories that make each of us who we are.
Your’s Sonderly is a collection of conversations with ordinary people — friends, acquaintances, and perhaps people I haven’t met yet — whose lives, experiences, perspectives, and stories I’m curious to explore and share.
Some conversations might be enlightening, some thought-provoking, and others simply fun. But at the heart of it all is a belief that everyone has a story worth hearing, something worth learning from, or simply something worth discovering.
The word Sonder, coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, describes the realization that every random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own, filled with their own ambitions, worries, relationships, memories, and experiences.
Sonderly is my little exploration of those lives, one conversation at a time. If you’d like to share your story, I would love to hear from you at **yourssonderly@gmail.com**.

author: Lexy Beard & Jamie Atkinson
description:
You'll hear us talking about the things we all experience but don't always say out loud: toxic workplaces, red & green flags, the chaos of adulthood, raising kids, marriage, mental load, and why folding a fitted sheet should qualify as an Olympic event.


And because sometimes venting is cheaper than therapy, we started this Podcast, where sarcasm is encouraged, honesty is celebrated, and perfection is absolutely not required. Let’s laugh through the chaos together!

Drawing on 30+ years as a professional hairstylist and experience in cosmetic formulation, Sakinah explores hair and scalp care, skin, menopause-related changes, product ingredients, beauty after 40, and everyday self-care.
Expect honest conversations, practical education, and a closer look at what your hair actually needs—beyond the marketing.
Because hair has context, and products do too. 👑

title: Moments With Brien
author: Brien Andrews
description:
Take a moment to meet God right where you are.


Moments with Brien is a devotional for real life. Each episode starts with an ordinary moment, like a quiet house at dinnertime, the Monday morning alarm, or a doctor's waiting room. Then we open God's Word to meet you right there.

Every episode includes:
• A Scripture reading 
• An honest reflection
• A guided prayer for you and for others carrying the same burden
• One simple takeaway to carry through your day

We talk honestly about loneliness, grief, fear, fresh starts, hard decisions, and more. You don't have to have it all together. Just come as you are, and stay as long as you need.

🔔 New episodes every Monday and Thursday. Subscribe and turn on notifications so you don't miss a moment.

If an episode encourages you, share it with someone who needs it today.

Be blessed.
Brien

Real stories, honest conversations

The My Military Lifestyle Podcast is a lifestyle show for military families, active-duty, reserves, retired, veterans, and everyone in between designed to make everyday military life less complicated and more enjoyable. In each episode we talk about tips, real-life guidance, and relatable stories covering the realities of military living, from PCS moves and finances to wellness, friendships, and self-care. Hosted by military lifestyle expert and community builder Rachel Slack, she explores all corners of the military lifestyle and creates a supportive space where listeners can laugh, cry and feel understood while gaining knowledgeable resources and information that may be useful to them.

When he isn't taking live calls, the tables turn because he and his in-studio guests are exchanging their own Chris vs. The People-esque stories. From first date horror stories to childhood regrets, there's always something to relate to and something to be absolutely stunned by. (Video episodes are available on YouTube)

title: Beyond The Physique: BMC Members Only Podcast
author: Bradley Makokha
description:
Build mental capacity, be more confident & bring meaningful change (just a few things I thought BMC could stand for). If you're here, you're already part of the BMC community and have made an investment in your health which I believe is something we should cherish and look after as best as possible for as long as we have time on this Earth. 

This podcast is different because you will be getting access to my unfiltered thoughts, experiences, challenges and new learnings as I grow as a coach in real time. Any new research, I'll talk about here first, any discoveries in my own training, you guessed it, here first. I want to build something using this podcast that genuinely leaves a lasting impact on anyone that tunes in. Whether that be you binge listen everything or have a favourite episode you repeat weekly, my mission is complete. 

In case you didn't know this already, I am more critical of myself than anyone else on this planet and that comes with a lot but this podcast will serve as a creative outlet for me (so much goes on in this brain of mine). One that can inspire, educate and mould you guys into thinking and operating with a growth mindset, because staying stagnant is not what you were put on this planet to do. I will challenge you to look inwards and reflect on the things that make you you as I think this is vital for all individuals throughout life. We'll cover all elements of the program, talk about life, goals, and even have group discussions and learnings from myself but also the community to develop as people over time. We're here to get into shape but also develop as people beyond that so welcome to beyond the physique, I hope you enjoy listening as much I enjoy making these episodes for you guys!

You're here because you're serious about your health so welcome to Beyond the Physcial, strap in.

Welcome to the dark side of human nature. 🔪

Explore the world's most disturbing true crime stories, shocking murders, mysterious disappearances, serial killers, criminal investigations, and real-life cases that reveal the darkest corners of humanity.

Each episode takes you deep into chilling details, twisted motives, unexpected evidence, and shocking revelations behind crimes that captured the world's attention.

From unbelievable murder cases to deeply disturbing criminal minds, we uncover the stories behind the headlines with compelling storytelling, detailed investigations, and suspenseful narration.

title: The Annals Of Time Docuseries
author: Rab
description:
https://linktr.ee/oneuptheannals

Welcome to The Annals Of Time Docuseries 


The Annals of Time is a cinematic narrative nonfiction docuseries that turns history, mystery, culture, crime, and the strange corners of the human story into immersive audio experiences.

Hosted by Rab Greeson and featuring Victoria, The Annals of Time isn't a traditional conversational podcast. Every episode is researched, scripted, performed, and built around music, sound design, humor, and dramatic storytelling to make the past feel less like something being explained and more like something happening around you.

One episode might descend into the tortured life of Edgar Allan Poe. Another might put Halloween on an autopsy table, trace the strange evolution of online dating, uncover how makeup became power and identity, or ask why something as simple as two people holding hands can carry thousands of years of meaning.

The subjects change.

The mission doesn't.

Find the extraordinary hiding inside the familiar.

Part documentary. Part storytelling. Part controlled chaos.

History wasn't boring when it happened.
We don't think it should sound boring now.

title: The Record

description:
The Record is a dramatized audio series. Each episode is performed from the official public record of a real event: cockpit and bridge voice-recorder transcripts, mission audio transcripts, hearing exhibits, and accident reports published by the National Transportation Safety Board, the United States Coast Guard, NASA, and other government bodies.

The voices you hear are actors. They are not the people who lived these events, and no recording of the actual people is used. Speech is performed as a script, not as an imitation.

description: Following Jesus doesn’t mean life gets simple. The First Few is a short daily Christian devotional with Aaron Powers, where we bring real struggles, honest questions, and everyday emotions into the light of Scripture. Together, we’ll look beyond surface-level encouragement and discover how Jesus meets us in the middle of real life. No pretending we’ve got it all figured out. Just a few meaningful minutes to hear God’s Word, examine our hearts, and take one step toward Him. Start your day with the first few minutes that matter.

Breaking news. Lasting questions.

Each episode starts from a verified story and asks what it reveals about justice, mercy, truth, power or responsibility. It then turns to the Qur'an, read in context and with recognised scholarship.

description:
Do you find yourself battling against overwhelm, exhaustion, anxiety, burnout, depression, or despair? Do you regularly beat yourself up over “losing it” with your kids? Wish you could shake the feeling that you’re failing as a mother? Want to finally wake up as the mom you so desperately want to be?
I’m so glad you’re here, mama. This podcast will help you address what you’re battling against at the source so that you can become the thriving, Christlike mom you long to be.
Hi, I’m Kristen: a wife, mother, Jesus-lover, and author of the book Mothering on Empty: How Moms Like You Found God’s Joy. I too have said “yes” in response to each of the questions I just asked above.
For years I struggled - as a mom, as a wife, and as a person. I blamed myself for everything that was “wrong” in my life - my children’s tantrums, the dysfunction in my marriage, and my inability to “get it together” emotionally. 
Finally, slowly, God began to show me that it wasn’t my fault - that the hurdles I felt surrounded by weren’t a result of “character flaws”, “lack of faith” or “not trying hard enough”. He helped me uncover root causes of my struggles and began to bring about healing and wholeness from the inside out.
As a result, He’s given me a newfound understanding of and passion for spiritual wellness. By His grace, He’s revealed how the health of my spirit impacts, and is influenced by, all the other aspects of my life & being. And now, I’m here to share what I’ve learned with you!
If you’re ready to gain insight into: 
why you seem to keep hitting the same brick walls; 
where your debilitating thoughts and feelings are actually stemming from; 
and how to start experiencing roots-deep transformation in your motherhood, 
then you’ve come to the right place.
Grab your boxing gloves, mama. It’s time to ditch defeat and take back what the Enemy’s stolen. Let’s reclaim your spirit’s health and get you on the path to the kind of victorious, fruitful motherhood our Heavenly Father wants for you!
Want to get your hands on a copy of the book Mothering on Empty? Visit the Meantime Mom website: www.meantimemom.com.
Looking for community and support? Join the free Meantime Mom Facebook group: Meantime Mom Sisterhood.

author: Don Shafer
description:
EROSIONS To See and See Again

A podcast with Minelle Mahtani

What happens slowly enough that we fail to notice? The gradual erosion of our relationships, our communities, our memories, and the stories we tell about ourselves. The quiet changes that shape our lives, often unnoticed until something—or someone—we love is gone.

In Erosions, writer, broadcaster, and scholar Minelle Mahtani sits down with remarkable authors and thinkers whose work challenges how we understand the world and our place within it. Through intimate, thoughtful, and sometimes unexpected conversations, Minelle explores the stories behind the stories. What compels a writer to write? What do they see that others overlook? How do questions of identity, belonging, injustice, memory, and love find their way onto the page?

And what can literature teach us about paying attention in a world that increasingly demands we look away? These are conversations about books, certainly. But they're also about the lives that produce them, the experiences that shape us, and the possibilities that emerge when we become willing to see—and see again. 

Because erosion isn't always about what disappears; sometimes, it's about what becomes visible when we finally pay attention.

**Every Movie Has a Story. Every Minute Has a Secret.**

Welcome to **Reel Crime: A Film Analysis Podcast**, where legendary crime films are examined one minute at a time!

From unforgettable characters and iconic performances to shocking betrayals, memorable dialogue, and behind-the-scenes secrets, we break down the movies that defined generations.

Each episode takes you deeper into a single minute of cinematic history, exploring the storytelling, filmmaking techniques, character motivations, hidden details, and cultural impact that make these films unforgettable.

Our journey begins with Brian De Palma's 1983 crime classic *Scarface*, starring Al Pacino as Tony Montana. We'll explore the film minute by minute, examining its characters, performances, production history, and lasting influence on popular culture.

Whether you're a lifelong movie enthusiast or discovering these classics for the first time, **Reel Crime** offers a fresh perspective on the films you thought you knew.

**One Movie. One Minute. Endless Stories.**

*Disclaimer: Reel Crime is an independent film criticism and commentary podcast. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by any motion picture studio, filmmaker, or copyright holder. All film titles and references are used for identification, discussion, and critical analysis.*

title: F*CK! I'M 50
author: Paul Burfitt
description:
F*CK! I’M 50 started with a pretty simple question: where the bloody hell did the last 20 years go?


One minute you’re busy working, raising kids and dealing with life, the next you wake up and realise — F*CK! I'm 50! Our kids hardly need us anymore, yet our parents need us more than ever before.


My name's Paul Burfitt. My mates call me Burf. I’m not a guru, not a life coach and certainly not an expert. I’m just a bloke from Queensland who’s decided I’m not going to keep putting everything off.


So I’m talking to people from around Australia and other places about all the stuff that comes up at this stage of life — family, money, health, work, relationships, ambitions, regrets, f*ck-ups, starting again and figuring out what makes you happy.


Some conversations will be with everyday people who have great stories. Others will be with people you already know from sport, media, business or somewhere completely unexpected. And every now and then I’ll bring in someone who genuinely knows a thing or two on the subject they’re talking.


I’ve got a podcast and a little YouTube channel set up. You’re invited to come along for the ride as I start ticking off a few things I’ve spent too many years saying I’d do “one day”.


I'm sure some people will think it's a brilliant idea. Plenty more probably won’t. But either way here we go, and remember this is a hate free zone so play nice…

There's sure to be some spills, thrills and the occasional disaster as I try to make up for a bit of lost time.


If the name of my show is a bit in your face - that's kind of the point - you can always refer to it as Fi50 too.


Most of all remember, F*CK! I’M 50 isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about finally asking the questions — and doing something about them.

**I Was Born Watching Scary Movies** is a horror movie podcast with no map, no master list, and no telling where we’ll end up.

Maybe it takes us to an old favorite, something we’ve never seen, or a movie we never expected to end up watching. We can move forward, double back, or wander off in a completely different direction. Where we go is anyone’s guess—the only rule is that the movie has to get us there.
But the journey from one movie to the next is only part of the fun. We’re here to watch scary movies, talk about them, and enjoy the conversation that follows. Classics, cult favorites, forgotten B-movies, new releases, masterpieces, disasters—there’s no telling what might come next.
So pick a seat, settle in, and follow the show. There are a lot of scary movies out there, and we’ve got a long way to go.

title: Law of Attraction Secrets
author: Law of Attraction Secrets
description:
What if the way you think about your day quietly shapes the way you experience it? Law of Attraction Secrets is a podcast of short, focused idea-episodes about thought, attention, and mindset. Each episode takes one simple idea, looks at it from a few angles, and leaves you with something to reflect on as you go about your life. No hype, no shortcuts, and no promises of instant change. Just clear, calm conversations about the inner side of everyday living.
WHAT THIS SHOW IS ABOUT
The phrase "law of attraction" means different things to different people. For some, it suggests a mysterious force. For others, it is simply a reminder that what we focus on tends to grow in our awareness. This show leans toward the practical and reflective end of that spectrum. We explore the idea that our thoughts, expectations, and habits of attention influence how we interpret events, which opportunities we notice, and how we respond when things do not go as planned.
Rather than treating attraction as a formula, we treat it as a lens. Through that lens, we ask useful questions. What am I paying attention to right now? What story am I telling myself about this situation? Which beliefs are guiding my choices without my noticing? These questions do not have one correct answer, and that is exactly why they are worth asking. The aim is not to control the world with our minds, but to become more aware of how our minds meet the world.
Every episode stands on its own. You do not need any background knowledge, special vocabulary, or previous episodes to follow along. You only need a few minutes and a willingness to think honestly about your own experience. Some ideas will resonate with you immediately. Others may feel unfamiliar at first and make more sense weeks later, when a situation in your life brings them back to mind.

HOW SHORT IDEA EPISODES WORK
Law of Attraction Secrets is built around short episodes, each centered on a single theme. One day we might look at the difference between wishing and intending. Another day we might explore why gratitude changes the texture of an ordinary afternoon, or how a single worried thought can grow into a whole imagined future. The format is deliberately compact, so you can listen during a commute, a walk, a coffee break, or the quiet minutes before sleep.
A typical episode moves through three simple steps. First, we introduce the idea in plain language. Second, we connect it to familiar situations: conversations at work, decisions at home, moments of doubt, moments of hope. Third, we offer a reflection question or a small practice you can try on your own. There is no homework and no pressure. The practice is an invitation, not an assignment.
Short episodes have a quiet advantage. Big ideas are often easier to absorb in small pieces. When a concept is presented briefly and clearly, it tends to stay with you longer. You may find yourself remembering a phrase or a question at an unexpected moment, and that moment of remembering is often where the real reflection begins.
THOUGHTS, ATTENTION, AND EVERYDAY LIFE
Much of what we call mindset is really a pattern of attention. Two people can walk down the same street and notice completely different things. One sees closed shops and grey skies; the other sees a friendly face, a new café, an interesting building. Neither is wrong. They are simply looking through different filters. This show spends a lot of time on those filters: where they come from, how they shape our mood, and how we can gently adjust them.
We look at everyday moments where thought and experience meet. The morning thought that sets the tone for the whole day. The habit of rehearsing difficult conversations before they happen. The tendency to expect disappointment so that we will not be surprised by it. The way a small success can change how we approach the next challenge. These are ordinary experiences, but they carry a lot of weight. Understanding them a little better can make daily life feel more intentional and less automatic.
It is important to say clearly what this show does not claim. Thinking positively does not make difficulties disappear, and no one is to blame for hardship simply because of their thoughts. Life includes loss, uncertainty, and circumstances far outside our control. What we explore here is the space we do have: how we pay attention, how we interpret what happens, and how we choose our next step. That space is often larger than we assume, and it is worth exploring with patience and honesty.
THE INNER HABITS WE EXPLORE
Across the episodes, a number of recurring themes appear. One is clarity: the practice of knowing what you actually want, rather than only what you want to avoid. It sounds simple, yet many of us spend more energy describing our fears than describing our hopes. Another is expectation: how our assumptions about what is likely to happen influence how we prepare, how we show up, and how we read the results.
We also explore gratitude, not as a forced exercise, but as a way of noticing what is already present and working. We look at self-talk, the inner voice that comments on everything we do, and how its tone can be softened without becoming dishonest. We spend time on patience, because meaningful change in habits and perspective usually unfolds slowly. We talk about letting go, which is different from giving up: it is the ability to hold an intention while releasing the need to control every detail.
Other episodes focus on visualization and imagination, the way we picture possible futures and how those pictures can either motivate us or overwhelm us. We discuss emotional awareness, recognizing feelings as signals rather than commands. We look at consistency, the small daily choices that quietly add up over time. And we return often to curiosity, perhaps the most useful inner habit of all, because it keeps us open to learning rather than stuck in fixed conclusions about ourselves and others.
WHO THIS IS FOR
This podcast is for anyone who is curious about the connection between inner life and outer experience. You might be new to the idea of the law of attraction and want a grounded, sensible introduction. You might have explored the topic before and want a calmer, more reflective perspective than the dramatic claims you sometimes encounter. Or you might simply enjoy short episodes that make you pause and think.
Listeners often include people going through transitions: starting a new job, moving to a new place, ending or beginning a relationship, or simply feeling that it is time for a fresh outlook. Others are students, creatives, parents, entrepreneurs, and professionals who want a few minutes of mental clarity in a busy day. You do not need to share any particular belief system to benefit. If you are open to examining your own thoughts with kindness and honesty, you are in the right place.
This show is also for skeptics. Healthy questioning is welcome here. You are encouraged to test every idea against your own experience, keep what is helpful, and set aside what is not. Reflection works best when it is personal and honest, not when it is accepted without thought.
HOW TO LISTEN AND USE THESE IDEAS
There is no right way to listen, but a few suggestions may help. Try choosing one episode and letting it be your theme for the day. Notice when the idea shows up in your conversations, your reactions, or your choices. You might write down the reflection question and return to it in the evening. Some listeners keep a simple notebook of ideas that stood out, which over time becomes a personal record of how their thinking has shifted.
It can also help to revisit episodes. An idea that sounded abstract the first time may feel very concrete after a challenging week. Because the episodes are short, replaying one is easy, and repetition often reveals details you missed. Feel free to share episodes with friends or family and talk about them together. Conversation is one of the best ways to turn an interesting idea into a lived understanding.
Above all, go at your own pace. These ideas are meant to support reflection, not to create pressure or unrealistic expectations. Results from any mindset practice vary from person to person, and no single approach fits everyone. Treat each episode as a small conversation with yourself, an opportunity to notice, question, and choose a little more consciously. Subscribe, press play when you need a moment of perspective, and see which ideas become your own.
Law of Attraction Secrets is educational and reflective — not a substitute for professional advice.
